newsitem.title: VANUATU: Vanuatu PM restructures coalition government.
newsitem.headline: Vanuatu PM restructures coalition government.

text.p: Vanuatu Prime Minister Serge Vohor has restructured his coalition government, dumping one party and reinstating two former colleagues, claiming it will ensure political stability in the South Pacific state.
Vanuatu has had a recent history of "revolving door" politics, with Vohor coming to power with a shaky coalition last September after a vote of no confidence in the then government.
"I am confident my party is now stable and the new government will be a stable one, and stability will prevail in Vanuatu," Vohor told reporters late on Wednesday.
The Vanuaaku Pati of deputy prime minister Donald Kalpokas was dropped from the ruling Union of Moderate Parties (UMP) coalition in a reshuffle on Tuesday, Vohor said.
Kalpokas' party has been replaced by former prime minister Maxime Carlot's UMP Natora faction and the Melanesian Progressive Party of Barak Sope, another former Vohor ally.

Sope replaces Kalpokas as deputy prime minister and was also named as minister for commerce and industry. Korman, who Vohor deposed as prime minister last year, was appointed minister for foreign affairs.
The National United Party remains the fourth coalition member in Vohor's government. Kalpokas' Vanuaaku Party is now the only opposition party in the 50-seat parliament.
